pretreatments.description: Liquid hot water pretreatment was carried out in a 500 ml stainless steel Parr reactor with a pressure limit of 345 bar. The vessel was filled with 30 g duckweed (dry weight) and 270 g distilled water. The temperature was ramped up to 150 °C within 15 min, followed by pressurization with nitrogen gas for 5 min. This chemical-thermal treatment affects substrate properties, including enzymatic activity and hydrolysis.

Prior to liquefaction, the duckweed was sterilized by autoclaving with 945 ml water for 30 min at 121 °C. This thermal treatment removes microorganisms and affects the substrate's microbial composition and enzymatic potential.

Enzymatic liquefaction and saccharification of the duckweed was performed in four 2-L flasks with 1 L total working volume. Prior to liquefaction, the duckweed was sterilized by autoclaving. pH was adjusted to 7.0 ± 0.1 with 2 M hydrochloric acid. α-amylase (5000 units g starch^-1) was added at 90 °C, followed by glucoamylase and cellulase. Saccharification was performed at 50 °C while mixing at 120 rpm for 24 h. This enzymatic-chemical treatment converts substrates into fermentable sugars, affecting substrate solubility and composition.
